paragraphs.text: After these things Jesus went away to the other side of the sea of Galilee, which is [the sea] of Tiberias.
paragraphs.original: Μετὰ ταῦτα ἀπῆλθεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς πέραν τῆς θαλάσσης τῆς Γαλιλαίας τῆς Τιβεριάδος.
paragraphs.translit: Meta tauta apēlthen ho Iēsous peran tēs thalassēs tēs Galilaias tēs Tiberiados.

paragraphs.text: And a great multitude followed him, because they beheld the signs which he did on them that were sick.
paragraphs.original: ἠκολούθει δὲ αὐτῷ ὄχλος πολύς, ὅτι ἐθεώρουν τὰ σημεῖα ἃ ἐποίει ἐπὶ τῶν ἀσθενούντων.
paragraphs.translit: ēkolouthei de autō ochlos polys, hoti etheōroun ta sēmeia ha epoiei epi tōn asthenountōn.

paragraphs.text: And Jesus went up into the mountain, and there he sat with his disciples.
paragraphs.original: ἀνῆλθεν δὲ εἰς τὸ ὄρος Ἰησοῦς, καὶ ἐκεῖ ἐκάθητο μετὰ τῶν μαθητῶν αὐτοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: anēlthen de eis to oros Iēsous, kai ekei ekathēto meta tōn mathētōn autou.

paragraphs.text: Now the passover, the feast of the Jews, was at hand.
paragraphs.original: ἦν δὲ ἐγγὺς τὸ πάσχα, ἡ ἑορτὴ τῶν Ἰουδαίων.
paragraphs.translit: ēn de engys to pascha, hē heortē tōn Ioudaiōn.

paragraphs.text: Jesus therefore lifting up his eyes, and seeing that a great multitude cometh unto him, saith unto Philip, Whence are we to buy bread, that these may eat?
paragraphs.original: ἐπάρας οὖν τοὺς ὀφθαλμοὺς ὁ Ἰησοῦς καὶ θεασάμενος ὅτι πολὺς ὄχλος ἔρχεται πρὸς αὐτὸν λέγει πρὸς Φίλιππον· Πόθεν ἀγοράσωμεν ἄρτους ἵνα φάγωσιν οὗτοι;
paragraphs.translit: eparas oun tous ophthalmous ho Iēsous kai theasamenos hoti polys ochlos erchetai pros auton legei pros Philippon· Pothen agorasōmen artous hina phagōsin houtoi;

paragraphs.text: And this he said to prove him: for he himself knew what he would do.
paragraphs.original: τοῦτο δὲ ἔλεγεν πειράζων αὐτόν, αὐτὸς γὰρ ᾔδει τί ἔμελλεν ποιεῖν.
paragraphs.translit: touto de elegen peirazōn auton, autos gar ēdei ti emellen poiein.

paragraphs.text: Philip answered him, Two hundred shillings` worth of bread is not sufficient for them, that every one may take a little.
paragraphs.original: ἀπεκρίθη αὐτῷ Φίλιππος· Διακοσίων δηναρίων ἄρτοι οὐκ ἀρκοῦσιν αὐτοῖς ἵνα ἕκαστος βραχύ τι λάβῃ.
paragraphs.translit: apekrithē autō Philippos· Diakosiōn dēnariōn artoi ouk arkousin autois hina hekastos brachy ti labē.

paragraphs.text: One of his disciples, Andrew, Simon Peter`s brother, saith unto him,
paragraphs.original: λέγει αὐτῷ εἷς ἐκ τῶν μαθητῶν αὐτοῦ, Ἀνδρέας ὁ ἀδελφὸς Σίμωνος Πέτρου·
paragraphs.translit: legei autō heis ek tōn mathētōn autou, Andreas ho adelphos Simōnos Petrou·

paragraphs.text: There is a lad here, who hath five barley loaves, and two fishes: but what are these among so many?
paragraphs.original: Ἔστιν παιδάριον ὧδε ὃς ἔχει πέντε ἄρτους κριθίνους καὶ δύο ὀψάρια· ἀλλὰ ταῦτα τί ἐστιν εἰς τοσούτους;
paragraphs.translit: Estin paidarion hōde hos echei pente artous krithinous kai dyo opsaria· alla tauta ti estin eis tosoutous;

paragraphs.text: Jesus said, Make the people sit down. Now there was much grass in the place. So the men sat down, in number about five thousand.
paragraphs.original: εἶπεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Ποιήσατε τοὺς ἀνθρώπους ἀναπεσεῖν. ἦν δὲ χόρτος πολὺς ἐν τῷ τόπῳ. ἀνέπεσαν οὖν οἱ ἄνδρες τὸν ἀριθμὸν ὡς πεντακισχίλιοι.
paragraphs.translit: eipen ho Iēsous· Poiēsate tous anthrōpous anapesein. ēn de chortos polys en tō topō. anepesan oun hoi andres ton arithmon hōs pentakischilioi.

paragraphs.text: Jesus therefore took the loaves; and having given thanks, he distributed to them that were set down; likewise also of the fishes as much as they would.
paragraphs.original: ἔλαβεν οὖν τοὺς ἄρτους ὁ Ἰησοῦς καὶ εὐχαριστήσας διέδωκεν τοῖς ἀνακειμένοις, ὁμοίως καὶ ἐκ τῶν ὀψαρίων ὅσον ἤθελον.
paragraphs.translit: elaben oun tous artous ho Iēsous kai eucharistēsas diedōken tois anakeimenois, homoiōs kai ek tōn opsariōn hoson ēthelon.

paragraphs.text: And when they were filled, he saith unto his disciples, Gather up the broken pieces which remain over, that nothing be lost.
paragraphs.original: ὡς δὲ ἐνεπλήσθησαν λέγει τοῖς μαθηταῖς αὐτοῦ· Συναγάγετε τὰ περισσεύσαντα κλάσματα, ἵνα μή τι ἀπόληται.
paragraphs.translit: hōs de eneplēsthēsan legei tois mathētais autou· Synagagete ta perisseusanta klasmata, hina mē ti apolētai.

paragraphs.text: So they gathered them up, and filled twelve baskets with broken pieces from the five barley loaves, which remained over unto them that had eaten.
paragraphs.original: συνήγαγον οὖν, καὶ ἐγέμισαν δώδεκα κοφίνους κλασμάτων ἐκ τῶν πέντε ἄρτων τῶν κριθίνων ἃ ἐπερίσσευσαν τοῖς βεβρωκόσιν.
paragraphs.translit: synēgagon oun, kai egemisan dōdeka kophinous klasmatōn ek tōn pente artōn tōn krithinōn ha eperisseusan tois bebrōkosin.

paragraphs.text: When therefore the people saw the sign which he did, they said, This is of a truth the prophet that cometh into the world.
paragraphs.original: οἱ οὖν ἄνθρωποι ἰδόντες ὃ ἐποίησεν σημεῖον ἔλεγον ὅτι Οὗτός ἐστιν ἀληθῶς ὁ προφήτης ὁ ἐρχόμενος εἰς τὸν κόσμον.
paragraphs.translit: hoi oun anthrōpoi idontes ho epoiēsen sēmeion elegon hoti Houtos estin alēthōs ho prophētēs ho erchomenos eis ton kosmon.

paragraphs.text: Jesus therefore perceiving that they were about to come and take him by force, to make him king, withdrew again into the mountain himself alone.
paragraphs.original: Ἰησοῦς οὖν γνοὺς ὅτι μέλλουσιν ἔρχεσθαι καὶ ἁρπάζειν αὐτὸν ἵνα ποιήσωσιν βασιλέα ἀνεχώρησεν πάλιν εἰς τὸ ὄρος αὐτὸς μόνος.
paragraphs.translit: Iēsous oun gnous hoti mellousin erchesthai kai harpazein auton hina poiēsōsin basilea anechōrēsen palin eis to oros autos monos.

paragraphs.text: And when evening came, his disciples went down unto the sea;
paragraphs.original: Ὡς δὲ ὀψία ἐγένετο κατέβησαν οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ ἐπὶ τὴν θάλασσαν,
paragraphs.translit: Hōs de opsia egeneto katebēsan hoi mathētai autou epi tēn thalassan,

paragraphs.text: and they entered into a boat, and were going over the sea unto Capernaum. And it was now dark, and Jesus had not yet come to them.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἐμβάντες εἰς πλοῖον ἤρχοντο πέραν τῆς θαλάσσης εἰς Καφαρναούμ. καὶ σκοτία ἤδη ἐγεγόνει καὶ οὔπω ἐληλύθει πρὸς αὐτοὺς ὁ Ἰησοῦς,
paragraphs.translit: kai embantes eis ploion ērchonto peran tēs thalassēs eis Kapharnaoum. kai skotia ēdē egegonei kai oupō elēlythei pros autous ho Iēsous,

paragraphs.text: And the sea was rising by reason of a great wind that blew.
paragraphs.original: ἥ τε θάλασσα ἀνέμου μεγάλου πνέοντος διεγείρετο.
paragraphs.translit: hē te thalassa anemou megalou pneontos diegeireto.

paragraphs.text: When therefore they had rowed about five and twenty or thirty furlongs, they behold Jesus walking on the sea, and drawing nigh unto the boat: and they were afraid.
paragraphs.original: ἐληλακότες οὖν ὡς σταδίους εἴκοσι πέντε ἢ τριάκοντα θεωροῦσιν τὸν Ἰησοῦν περιπατοῦντα ἐπὶ τῆς θαλάσσης καὶ ἐγγὺς τοῦ πλοίου γινόμενον, καὶ ἐφοβήθησαν.
paragraphs.translit: elēlakotes oun hōs stadious eikosi pente ē triakonta theōrousin ton Iēsoun peripatounta epi tēs thalassēs kai engys tou ploiou ginomenon, kai ephobēthēsan.

paragraphs.text: But he saith unto them, It is I; be not afraid.
paragraphs.original: ὁ δὲ λέγει αὐτοῖς· Ἐγώ εἰμι, μὴ φοβεῖσθε.
paragraphs.translit: ho de legei autois· Egō eimi, mē phobeisthe.

paragraphs.text: They were willing therefore to receive him into the boat: and straightway the boat was at the land whither they were going.
paragraphs.original: ἤθελον οὖν λαβεῖν αὐτὸν εἰς τὸ πλοῖον, καὶ εὐθέως ἐγένετο τὸ πλοῖον ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς εἰς ἣν ὑπῆγον.
paragraphs.translit: ēthelon oun labein auton eis to ploion, kai eutheōs egeneto to ploion epi tēs gēs eis hēn hypēgon.

paragraphs.text: On the morrow the multitude that stood on the other side of the sea saw that there was no other boat there, save one, and that Jesus entered not with his disciples into the boat, but [that] his disciples went away alone
paragraphs.original: Τῇ ἐπαύριον ὁ ὄχλος ὁ ἑστηκὼς πέραν τῆς θαλάσσης εἶδον ὅτι πλοιάριον ἄλλο οὐκ ἦν ἐκεῖ εἰ μὴ ἕν, καὶ ὅτι οὐ συνεισῆλθεν τοῖς μαθηταῖς αὐτοῦ ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἰς τὸ πλοῖον ἀλλὰ μόνοι οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ ἀπῆλθον·
paragraphs.translit: Tē epaurion ho ochlos ho hestēkōs peran tēs thalassēs eidon hoti ploiarion allo ouk ēn ekei ei mē hen, kai hoti ou syneisēlthen tois mathētais autou ho Iēsous eis to ploion alla monoi hoi mathētai autou apēlthon·

paragraphs.text: (howbeit there came boats from Tiberias nigh unto the place where they ate the bread after the Lord had given thanks):
paragraphs.original: ἀλλὰ ἦλθεν πλοιάρια ἐκ Τιβεριάδος ἐγγὺς τοῦ τόπου ὅπου ἔφαγον τὸν ἄρτον εὐχαριστήσαντος τοῦ κυρίου.
paragraphs.translit: alla ēlthen ploiaria ek Tiberiados engys tou topou hopou ephagon ton arton eucharistēsantos tou kyriou.

paragraphs.text: when the multitude therefore saw that Jesus was not there, neither his disciples, they themselves got into the boats, and came to Capernaum, seeking Jesus.
paragraphs.original: ὅτε οὖν εἶδεν ὁ ὄχλος ὅτι Ἰησοῦς οὐκ ἔστιν ἐκεῖ οὐδὲ οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ, ἐνέβησαν αὐτοὶ εἰς τὰ πλοιάρια καὶ ἦλθον εἰς Καφαρναοὺμ ζητοῦντες τὸν Ἰησοῦν.
paragraphs.translit: hote oun eiden ho ochlos hoti Iēsous ouk estin ekei oude hoi mathētai autou, enebēsan autoi eis ta ploiaria kai ēlthon eis Kapharnaoum zētountes ton Iēsoun.

paragraphs.text: And when they found him on the other side of the sea, they said unto him, Rabbi, when camest thou hither?
paragraphs.original: Καὶ εὑρόντες αὐτὸν πέραν τῆς θαλάσσης εἶπον αὐτῷ· Ῥαββί, πότε ὧδε γέγονας;
paragraphs.translit: Kai heurontes auton peran tēs thalassēs eipon autō· Rhabbi, pote hōde gegonas;

paragraphs.text: Jesus answered them and said, Verily, verily, I say unto you, Ye seek me, not because ye saw signs, but because ye ate of the loaves, and were filled.
paragraphs.original: ἀπεκρίθη αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς καὶ εἶπεν· Ἀμὴν ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν, ζητεῖτέ με οὐχ ὅτι εἴδετε σημεῖα ἀλλʼ ὅτι ἐφάγετε ἐκ τῶν ἄρτων καὶ ἐχορτάσθητε·
paragraphs.translit: apekrithē autois ho Iēsous kai eipen· Amēn amēn legō hymin, zēteite me ouch hoti eidete sēmeia allʼ hoti ephagete ek tōn artōn kai echortasthēte·

paragraphs.text: Work not for the food which perisheth, but for the food which abideth unto eternal life, which the Son of man shall give unto you: for him the Father, even God, hath sealed.
paragraphs.original: ἐργάζεσθε μὴ τὴν βρῶσιν τὴν ἀπολλυμένην ἀλλὰ τὴν βρῶσιν τὴν μένουσαν εἰς ζωὴν αἰώνιον, ἣν ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ὑμῖν δώσει, τοῦτον γὰρ ὁ πατὴρ ἐσφράγισεν ὁ θεός.
paragraphs.translit: ergazesthe mē tēn brōsin tēn apollymenēn alla tēn brōsin tēn menousan eis zōēn aiōnion, hēn ho hyios tou anthrōpou hymin dōsei, touton gar ho patēr esphragisen ho theos.

paragraphs.text: They said therefore unto him, What must we do, that we may work the works of God?
paragraphs.original: εἶπον οὖν πρὸς αὐτόν· Τί ποιῶμεν ἵνα ἐργαζώμεθα τὰ ἔργα τοῦ θεοῦ;
paragraphs.translit: eipon oun pros auton· Ti poiōmen hina ergazōmetha ta erga tou theou;

paragraphs.text: Jesus answered and said unto them, This is the work of God, that ye believe on him whom he hath sent.
paragraphs.original: ἀπεκρίθη ὁ Ἰησοῦς καὶ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Τοῦτό ἐστιν τὸ ἔργον τοῦ θεοῦ ἵνα πιστεύητε εἰς ὃν ἀπέστειλεν ἐκεῖνος.
paragraphs.translit: apekrithē ho Iēsous kai eipen autois· Touto estin to ergon tou theou hina pisteuēte eis hon apesteilen ekeinos.

paragraphs.text: They said therefore unto him, What then doest thou for a sign, that we may see, and believe thee? what workest thou?
paragraphs.original: εἶπον οὖν αὐτῷ· Τί οὖν ποιεῖς σὺ σημεῖον, ἵνα ἴδωμεν καὶ πιστεύσωμέν σοι; τί ἐργάζῃ;
paragraphs.translit: eipon oun autō· Ti oun poieis sy sēmeion, hina idōmen kai pisteusōmen soi; ti ergazē;

paragraphs.text: Our fathers ate the manna in the wilderness; as it is written, He gave them bread out of heaven to eat.
paragraphs.original: οἱ πατέρες ἡμῶν τὸ μάννα ἔφαγον ἐν τῇ ἐρήμῳ, καθώς ἐστιν γεγραμμένον· Ἄρτον ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ ἔδωκεν αὐτοῖς φαγεῖν.
paragraphs.translit: hoi pateres hēmōn to manna ephagon en tē erēmō, kathōs estin gegrammenon· Arton ek tou ouranou edōken autois phagein.

paragraphs.text: Jesus therefore said unto them, Verily, verily, I say unto you, It was not Moses that gave you the bread out of heaven; but my Father giveth you the true bread out of heaven.
paragraphs.original: εἶπεν οὖν αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Ἀμὴν ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν, οὐ Μωϋσῆς δέδωκεν ὑμῖν τὸν ἄρτον ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ, ἀλλʼ ὁ πατήρ μου δίδωσιν ὑμῖν τὸν ἄρτον ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ τὸν ἀληθινόν·
paragraphs.translit: eipen oun autois ho Iēsous· Amēn amēn legō hymin, ou Mōysēs dedōken hymin ton arton ek tou ouranou, allʼ ho patēr mou didōsin hymin ton arton ek tou ouranou ton alēthinon·

paragraphs.text: For the bread of God is that which cometh down out of heaven, and giveth life unto the world.
paragraphs.original: ὁ γὰρ ἄρτος τοῦ θεοῦ ἐστιν ὁ καταβαίνων ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ καὶ ζωὴν διδοὺς τῷ κόσμῳ.
paragraphs.translit: ho gar artos tou theou estin ho katabainōn ek tou ouranou kai zōēn didous tō kosmō.

paragraphs.text: They said therefore unto him, Lord, evermore give us this bread.
paragraphs.original: εἶπον οὖν πρὸς αὐτόν· Κύριε, πάντοτε δὸς ἡμῖν τὸν ἄρτον τοῦτον.
paragraphs.translit: eipon oun pros auton· Kyrie, pantote dos hēmin ton arton touton.

paragraphs.text: Jesus said unto them. I am the bread of life: he that cometh to me shall not hunger, and he that believeth on me shall never thirst.
paragraphs.original: Εἶπεν αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Ἐγώ εἰμι ὁ ἄρτος τῆς ζωῆς· ὁ ἐρχόμενος πρὸς ἐμὲ οὐ μὴ πεινάσῃ, καὶ ὁ πιστεύων εἰς ἐμὲ οὐ μὴ διψήσει πώποτε.
paragraphs.translit: Eipen autois ho Iēsous· Egō eimi ho artos tēs zōēs· ho erchomenos pros eme ou mē peinasē, kai ho pisteuōn eis eme ou mē dipsēsei pōpote.

paragraphs.text: But I said unto you, that ye have seen me, and yet believe not.
paragraphs.original: ἀλλʼ εἶπον ὑμῖν ὅτι καὶ ἑωράκατέ με καὶ οὐ πιστεύετε.
paragraphs.translit: allʼ eipon hymin hoti kai heōrakate me kai ou pisteuete.

paragraphs.text: All that which the Father giveth me shall come unto me; and him that cometh to me I will in no wise cast out.
paragraphs.original: πᾶν ὃ δίδωσίν μοι ὁ πατὴρ πρὸς ἐμὲ ἥξει, καὶ τὸν ἐρχόμενον πρός με οὐ μὴ ἐκβάλω ἔξω,
paragraphs.translit: pan ho didōsin moi ho patēr pros eme hēxei, kai ton erchomenon pros me ou mē ekbalō exō,

paragraphs.text: For I am come down from heaven, not to do mine own will, but the will of him that sent me.
paragraphs.original: ὅτι καταβέβηκα ἀπὸ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ οὐχ ἵνα ποιῶ τὸ θέλημα τὸ ἐμὸν ἀλλὰ τὸ θέλημα τοῦ πέμψαντός με·
paragraphs.translit: hoti katabebēka apo tou ouranou ouch hina poiō to thelēma to emon alla to thelēma tou pempsantos me·

paragraphs.text: And this is the will of him that sent me, that of all that which he hath given me I should lose nothing, but should raise it up at the last day.
paragraphs.original: τοῦτο δέ ἐστιν τὸ θέλημα τοῦ πέμψαντός με ἵνα πᾶν ὃ δέδωκέν μοι μὴ ἀπολέσω ἐξ αὐτοῦ ἀλλὰ ἀναστήσω αὐτὸ τῇ ἐσχάτῃ ἡμέρᾳ.
paragraphs.translit: touto de estin to thelēma tou pempsantos me hina pan ho dedōken moi mē apolesō ex autou alla anastēsō auto tē eschatē hēmera.

paragraphs.text: For this is the will of my Father, that every one that beholdeth the Son, and believeth on him, should have eternal life; and I will raise him up at the last day.
paragraphs.original: τοῦτο γάρ ἐστιν τὸ θέλημα τοῦ πατρός μου ἵνα πᾶς ὁ θεωρῶν τὸν υἱὸν καὶ πιστεύων εἰς αὐτὸν ἔχῃ ζωὴν αἰώνιον, καὶ ἀναστήσω αὐτὸν ἐγὼ τῇ ἐσχάτῃ ἡμέρᾳ.
paragraphs.translit: touto gar estin to thelēma tou patros mou hina pas ho theōrōn ton hyion kai pisteuōn eis auton echē zōēn aiōnion, kai anastēsō auton egō tē eschatē hēmera.

paragraphs.text: The Jews therefore murmured concerning him, because he said, I am the bread which came down out of heaven.
paragraphs.original: Ἐγόγγυζον οὖν οἱ Ἰουδαῖοι περὶ αὐτοῦ ὅτι εἶπεν· Ἐγώ εἰμι ὁ ἄρτος ὁ καταβὰς ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ,
paragraphs.translit: Egongyzon oun hoi Ioudaioi peri autou hoti eipen· Egō eimi ho artos ho katabas ek tou ouranou,

paragraphs.text: And they said, Is not this Jesus, the son of Joseph, whose father and mother we know? how doth he now say, I am come down out of heaven?
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἔλεγον· Οὐχ οὗτός ἐστιν Ἰησοῦς ὁ υἱὸς Ἰωσήφ, οὗ ἡμεῖς οἴδαμεν τὸν πατέρα καὶ τὴν μητέρα; πῶς νῦν λέγει ὅτι Ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ καταβέβηκα;
paragraphs.translit: kai elegon· Ouch houtos estin Iēsous ho hyios Iōsēph, hou hēmeis oidamen ton patera kai tēn mētera; pōs nyn legei hoti Ek tou ouranou katabebēka;

paragraphs.text: Jesus answered and said unto them, Murmur not among yourselves.
paragraphs.original: ἀπεκρίθη Ἰησοῦς καὶ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Μὴ γογγύζετε μετʼ ἀλλήλων.
paragraphs.translit: apekrithē Iēsous kai eipen autois· Mē gongyzete metʼ allēlōn.

paragraphs.text: No man can come to me, except the Father that sent me draw him: and I will raise him up in the last day.
paragraphs.original: οὐδεὶς δύναται ἐλθεῖν πρός με ἐὰν μὴ ὁ πατὴρ ὁ πέμψας με ἑλκύσῃ αὐτόν, κἀγὼ ἀναστήσω αὐτὸν ἐν τῇ ἐσχάτῃ ἡμέρᾳ.
paragraphs.translit: oudeis dynatai elthein pros me ean mē ho patēr ho pempsas me helkysē auton, kagō anastēsō auton en tē eschatē hēmera.

paragraphs.text: It is written in the prophets, And they shall all be taught of God. Every one that hath heard from the Father, and hath learned, cometh unto me.
paragraphs.original: ἔστιν γεγραμμένον ἐν τοῖς προφήταις· Καὶ ἔσονται πάντες διδακτοὶ θεοῦ· πᾶς ὁ ἀκούσας παρὰ τοῦ πατρὸς καὶ μαθὼν ἔρχεται πρὸς ἐμέ.
paragraphs.translit: estin gegrammenon en tois prophētais· Kai esontai pantes didaktoi theou· pas ho akousas para tou patros kai mathōn erchetai pros eme.

paragraphs.text: Not that any man hath seen the Father, save he that is from God, he hath seen the Father.
paragraphs.original: οὐχ ὅτι τὸν πατέρα ἑώρακέν τις εἰ μὴ ὁ ὢν παρὰ τοῦ θεοῦ, οὗτος ἑώρακεν τὸν πατέρα.
paragraphs.translit: ouch hoti ton patera heōraken tis ei mē ho ōn para tou theou, houtos heōraken ton patera.

paragraphs.text: Verily, verily, I say unto you, He that believeth hath eternal life.
paragraphs.original: ἀμὴν ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν, ὁ πιστεύων ἔχει ζωὴν αἰώνιον.
paragraphs.translit: amēn amēn legō hymin, ho pisteuōn echei zōēn aiōnion.

paragraphs.text: I am the bread of life.
paragraphs.original: ἐγώ εἰμι ὁ ἄρτος τῆς ζωῆς·
paragraphs.translit: egō eimi ho artos tēs zōēs·

paragraphs.text: Your fathers ate the manna in the wilderness, and they died.
paragraphs.original: οἱ πατέρες ὑμῶν ἔφαγον ἐν τῇ ἐρήμῳ τὸ μάννα καὶ ἀπέθανον·
paragraphs.translit: hoi pateres hymōn ephagon en tē erēmō to manna kai apethanon·

paragraphs.text: This is the bread which cometh down out of heaven, that a man may eat thereof, and not die.
paragraphs.original: οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ ἄρτος ὁ ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ καταβαίνων ἵνα τις ἐξ αὐτοῦ φάγῃ καὶ μὴ ἀποθάνῃ·
paragraphs.translit: houtos estin ho artos ho ek tou ouranou katabainōn hina tis ex autou phagē kai mē apothanē·

paragraphs.text: I am the living bread which came down out of heaven: if any man eat of this bread, he shall live for ever: yea and the bread which I will give is my flesh, for the life of the world.
paragraphs.original: ἐγώ εἰμι ὁ ἄρτος ὁ ζῶν ὁ ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ καταβάς· ἐάν τις φάγῃ ἐκ τούτου τοῦ ἄρτου ζήσει εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα, καὶ ὁ ἄρτος δὲ ὃν ἐγὼ δώσω ἡ σάρξ μού ἐστιν ὑπὲρ τῆς τοῦ κόσμου ζωῆς.
paragraphs.translit: egō eimi ho artos ho zōn ho ek tou ouranou katabas· ean tis phagē ek toutou tou artou zēsei eis ton aiōna, kai ho artos de hon egō dōsō hē sarx mou estin hyper tēs tou kosmou zōēs.

paragraphs.text: The Jews therefore strove one with another, saying, How can this man give us his flesh to eat?
paragraphs.original: Ἐμάχοντο οὖν πρὸς ἀλλήλους οἱ Ἰουδαῖοι λέγοντες· Πῶς δύναται οὗτος ἡμῖν δοῦναι τὴν σάρκα αὐτοῦ φαγεῖν;
paragraphs.translit: Emachonto oun pros allēlous hoi Ioudaioi legontes· Pōs dynatai houtos hēmin dounai tēn sarka autou phagein;

paragraphs.text: Jesus therefore said unto them, Verily, verily, I say unto you, Except ye eat the flesh of the Son of man and drink his blood, ye have not life in yourselves.
paragraphs.original: εἶπεν οὖν αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Ἀμὴν ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν, ἐὰν μὴ φάγητε τὴν σάρκα τοῦ υἱοῦ τοῦ ἀνθρώπου καὶ πίητε αὐτοῦ τὸ αἷμα, οὐκ ἔχετε ζωὴν ἐν ἑαυτοῖς.
paragraphs.translit: eipen oun autois ho Iēsous· Amēn amēn legō hymin, ean mē phagēte tēn sarka tou hyiou tou anthrōpou kai piēte autou to haima, ouk echete zōēn en heautois.

paragraphs.text: He that eateth my flesh and drinketh my blood hath eternal life: and I will raise him up at the last day.
paragraphs.original: ὁ τρώγων μου τὴν σάρκα καὶ πίνων μου τὸ αἷμα ἔχει ζωὴν αἰώνιον, κἀγὼ ἀναστήσω αὐτὸν τῇ ἐσχάτῃ ἡμέρᾳ.
paragraphs.translit: ho trōgōn mou tēn sarka kai pinōn mou to haima echei zōēn aiōnion, kagō anastēsō auton tē eschatē hēmera.

paragraphs.text: For my flesh is meat indeed, and my blood is drink indeed.
paragraphs.original: ἡ γὰρ σάρξ μου ἀληθής ἐστι βρῶσις, καὶ τὸ αἷμά μου ἀληθής ἐστι πόσις.
paragraphs.translit: hē gar sarx mou alēthēs esti brōsis, kai to haima mou alēthēs esti posis.

paragraphs.text: He that eateth my flesh and drinketh my blood abideth in me, and I in him.
paragraphs.original: ὁ τρώγων μου τὴν σάρκα καὶ πίνων μου τὸ αἷμα ἐν ἐμοὶ μένει κἀγὼ ἐν αὐτῷ.
paragraphs.translit: ho trōgōn mou tēn sarka kai pinōn mou to haima en emoi menei kagō en autō.

paragraphs.text: As the living Father sent me, and I live because of the Father; so he that eateth me, he also shall live because of me.
paragraphs.original: καθὼς ἀπέστειλέν με ὁ ζῶν πατὴρ κἀγὼ ζῶ διὰ τὸν πατέρα, καὶ ὁ τρώγων με κἀκεῖνος ζήσει διʼ ἐμέ.
paragraphs.translit: kathōs apesteilen me ho zōn patēr kagō zō dia ton patera, kai ho trōgōn me kakeinos zēsei diʼ eme.

paragraphs.text: This is the bread which came down out of heaven: not as the fathers ate, and died; he that eateth this bread shall live for ever.
paragraphs.original: οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ ἄρτος ὁ ἐξ οὐρανοῦ καταβάς, οὐ καθὼς ἔφαγον οἱ πατέρες καὶ ἀπέθανον· ὁ τρώγων τοῦτον τὸν ἄρτον ζήσει εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα.
paragraphs.translit: houtos estin ho artos ho ex ouranou katabas, ou kathōs ephagon hoi pateres kai apethanon· ho trōgōn touton ton arton zēsei eis ton aiōna.

paragraphs.text: These things said he in the synagogue, as he taught in Capernaum.
paragraphs.original: ταῦτα εἶπεν ἐν συναγωγῇ διδάσκων ἐν Καφαρναούμ.
paragraphs.translit: tauta eipen en synagōgē didaskōn en Kapharnaoum.

paragraphs.text: Many therefore of his disciples, when the heard [this], said, This is a hard saying; who can hear it?
paragraphs.original: Πολλοὶ οὖν ἀκούσαντες ἐκ τῶν μαθητῶν αὐτοῦ εἶπαν· Σκληρός ἐστιν ὁ λόγος οὗτος· τίς δύναται αὐτοῦ ἀκούειν;
paragraphs.translit: Polloi oun akousantes ek tōn mathētōn autou eipan· Sklēros estin ho logos houtos· tis dynatai autou akouein;

paragraphs.text: But Jesus knowing in himself that his disciples murmured at this, said unto them, Doth this cause you to stumble?
paragraphs.original: εἰδὼς δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἐν ἑαυτῷ ὅτι γογγύζουσιν περὶ τούτου οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Τοῦτο ὑμᾶς σκανδαλίζει;
paragraphs.translit: eidōs de ho Iēsous en heautō hoti gongyzousin peri toutou hoi mathētai autou eipen autois· Touto hymas skandalizei;

paragraphs.text: [What] then if ye should behold the Son of man ascending where he was before?
paragraphs.original: ἐὰν οὖν θεωρῆτε τὸν υἱὸν τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἀναβαίνοντα ὅπου ἦν τὸ πρότερον;
paragraphs.translit: ean oun theōrēte ton hyion tou anthrōpou anabainonta hopou ēn to proteron;

paragraphs.text: It is the spirit that giveth life; the flesh profiteth nothing: the words that I have spoken unto you are spirit, are are life.
paragraphs.original: τὸ πνεῦμά ἐστιν τὸ ζῳοποιοῦν, ἡ σὰρξ οὐκ ὠφελεῖ οὐδέν· τὰ ῥήματα ἃ ἐγὼ λελάληκα ὑμῖν πνεῦμά ἐστιν καὶ ζωή ἐστιν.
paragraphs.translit: to pneuma estin to zōopoioun, hē sarx ouk ōphelei ouden· ta rhēmata ha egō lelalēka hymin pneuma estin kai zōē estin.

paragraphs.text: But there are some of you that believe not. For Jesus knew from the beginning who they were that believed not, and who it was that should betray him.
paragraphs.original: ἀλλὰ εἰσὶν ἐξ ὑμῶν τινες οἳ οὐ πιστεύουσιν. ᾔδει γὰρ ἐξ ἀρχῆς ὁ Ἰησοῦς τίνες εἰσὶν οἱ μὴ πιστεύοντες καὶ τίς ἐστιν ὁ παραδώσων αὐτόν.
paragraphs.translit: alla eisin ex hymōn tines hoi ou pisteuousin. ēdei gar ex archēs ho Iēsous tines eisin hoi mē pisteuontes kai tis estin ho paradōsōn auton.

paragraphs.text: And he said, For this cause have I said unto you, that no man can come unto me, except it be given unto him of the Father.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἔλεγεν· Διὰ τοῦτο εἴρηκα ὑμῖν ὅτι οὐδεὶς δύναται ἐλθεῖν πρός με ἐὰν μὴ ᾖ δεδομένον αὐτῷ ἐκ τοῦ πατρός.
paragraphs.translit: kai elegen· Dia touto eirēka hymin hoti oudeis dynatai elthein pros me ean mē ē dedomenon autō ek tou patros.

paragraphs.text: Upon this many of his disciples went back, and walked no more with him.
paragraphs.original: Ἐκ τούτου πολλοὶ ἐκ τῶν μαθητῶν αὐτοῦ ἀπῆλθον εἰς τὰ ὀπίσω καὶ οὐκέτι μετʼ αὐτοῦ περιεπάτουν.
paragraphs.translit: Ek toutou polloi ek tōn mathētōn autou apēlthon eis ta opisō kai ouketi metʼ autou periepatoun.

paragraphs.text: Jesus said therefore unto the twelve, Would ye also go away?
paragraphs.original: εἶπεν οὖν ὁ Ἰησοῦς τοῖς δώδεκα· Μὴ καὶ ὑμεῖς θέλετε ὑπάγειν;
paragraphs.translit: eipen oun ho Iēsous tois dōdeka· Mē kai hymeis thelete hypagein;

paragraphs.text: Simon Peter answered him, Lord, to whom shall we go? thou hast the words of eternal life.
paragraphs.original: ἀπεκρίθη αὐτῷ Σίμων Πέτρος· Κύριε, πρὸς τίνα ἀπελευσόμεθα; ῥήματα ζωῆς αἰωνίου ἔχεις,
paragraphs.translit: apekrithē autō Simōn Petros· Kyrie, pros tina apeleusometha; rhēmata zōēs aiōniou echeis,

paragraphs.text: And we have believed and know that thou art the Holy One of God.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἡμεῖς πεπιστεύκαμεν καὶ ἐγνώκαμεν ὅτι σὺ εἶ ὁ ἅγιος τοῦ θεοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: kai hēmeis pepisteukamen kai egnōkamen hoti sy ei ho hagios tou theou.

paragraphs.text: Jesus answered them, Did not I choose you the twelve, and one of you is a devil?
paragraphs.original: ἀπεκρίθη αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Οὐκ ἐγὼ ὑμᾶς τοὺς δώδεκα ἐξελεξάμην; καὶ ἐξ ὑμῶν εἷς διάβολός ἐστιν.
paragraphs.translit: apekrithē autois ho Iēsous· Ouk egō hymas tous dōdeka exelexamēn; kai ex hymōn heis diabolos estin.

paragraphs.text: Now he spake of Judas [the son] of Simon Iscariot, for he it was that should betray him, [being] one of the twelve.
paragraphs.original: ἔλεγεν δὲ τὸν Ἰούδαν Σίμωνος Ἰσκαριώτου· οὗτος γὰρ ἔμελλεν παραδιδόναι αὐτόν, εἷς ἐκ τῶν δώδεκα.
paragraphs.translit: elegen de ton Ioudan Simōnos Iskariōtou· houtos gar emellen paradidonai auton, heis ek tōn dōdeka.
